messages.content: What is the evolutionary history of pandas?

message.content: Pandas belong to the family Ursidae (bears). Their lineage diverged from other bears around 20–25 million years ago during the Miocene epoch. Fossil evidence shows that early bear ancestors were omnivorous and adapted to forested environments. Over time, some lineages evolved specialized diets; the giant panda’s ancestors gradually shifted toward bamboo consumption, which required morphological adaptations such as a pseudo‑thumb for grasping bamboo shoots. The modern giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) emerged roughly 2–3 million years ago, with its distinctive black‑and‑white coloration and bamboo‑specialized digestive system evolving as adaptations to its niche in temperate forests of China.
